kinds.d: Long wooden staff, about the user's height or more, used as a weapon and in martial arts training.

x.d: Okinawan six-foot staff, often tapered at the ends and traditionally of red or white oak; the 'king' of kobudō weapons.
Chinese staff about the user's height, thick at the base and thinner at the tip; one of the four major wushu weapons.

v.d: southern staff event in competitive wushu

x.d: English hardwood staff of 6–9 ft, sometimes tipped with metal; now used in stage combat and historical fencing.

kinds.d: Japanese wooden staff about 1.27 m long, used in jōdō and aiki-jō.

kinds.a: baston · kali sticks · arnis sticks · yantok
kinds.d: Pair or single stick of rattan or hardwood, about 66–76 cm long, used in Filipino martial arts.
Two short sticks joined by a cord or chain.
Baton with a side handle set at right angles to the shaft, used in pairs.
Metal truncheon with a central rod and two curved side prongs, used in pairs.

x.d: Sai with one side prong reversed, developed by Taira Shinken.

kinds.d: Short-handled sickle blade made as a weapon, often used in pairs. A garden sickle is in Garden & Grounds.
Three staff sections joined end to end by chains or cords.
Dart or blade on the end of a long rope, swung and cast.
Jointed steel segments ending in a dart, swung as a whip.
